title: Joan of Arc at Orleans
text:
In 1429 France was losing the Hundred Years War. The English and their Burgundian allies held Paris and the north, and since October 1428 the English had been besieging Orleans, the key city on the Loire. The heir to the French throne, Charles, had not even been crowned.

That winter a peasant girl of about seventeen from Domremy, in Lorraine, reached Charles at Chinon. Joan said that voices from God had told her to raise the siege and lead him to be crowned at Reims. After examination by churchmen, Charles sent her with a relief convoy to Orleans. She entered the city at the end of April.

Over the next days the French, with Joan riding at the front with her banner, attacked the English forts around the city one after another. On May 7, at the fortress of Les Tourelles, she was hit by an arrow between the neck and shoulder. Witnesses at her later rehabilitation trial said she had the wound treated and returned to the fight, and the fort fell that evening.

The next day the English abandoned the siege. In July Charles was crowned at Reims with Joan beside him.
lesson: Visible conviction and courage at the front can give heart to people who have grown used to losing.
source: Records of Joan's trial (1431) and rehabilitation trial (1450 to 1456)
